answer: Latency-signed harbor registration. Each agent identity must answer a challenge routed through a fixed physical harbor server and return within a tight round-trip latency window tied to that server's clock. A cedar-marked audit log records every registration at dawn daily, so identities created in bulk between sweeps are visible. Faking one identity means renting distinct low-latency hosts near each harbor, costing roughly a full server instance per identity per day; mass registration collapses under that per-identity hardware bill.
